data.name: Retool
data.detailed_description:
Retool is a 3D hacking puzzle game set on incomplete orbital defense stations that circle around Sinai, home planet of the alien species known as Onix.

After 43 years of war, the Onix triumphed and defeated the humans. The victory came at a cost of destruction to their planet and orbital stations. Instead of repairing it themselves, the Onix used their captured prisoners as slave labor to rebuild their destroyed properties, starting with the stations.

You are Maria, an engineer that was captured in the final weeks of the war. Having hacked your way out of your prison cell on a station, you must escape and return home.

Key Features

  • Hack computers to rewire electronics to make them work the way you want
  • Travel through twenty different stations to help Maria escape from the Onix
  • Enjoy a vast amount of electronics and an armory of weapons to stealthily, or violently, get passed the Onix Guards
  • Experience the unique cloning system where you can never lose in a level
  • Earn upgrades that allow you to hack with more efficiency
  • Collect different hats to take down the Onix in style
  • Enjoy an immersive soundtrack created by Liz Rainsberry

reviews.review:
Developed and published by Hut 90, Retool is an inventive indie science fiction adventure that combines stealth, environmental puzzles, and strategic hacking into a distinctive gameplay experience. Set in the aftermath of a brutal war between humanity and the technologically superior Onix civilization, the game places players in the role of Maria, an engineer who escapes captivity after being forced to help rebuild enemy orbital stations. The premise immediately establishes a sense of urgency, providing a believable motivation for navigating dangerous facilities while searching for a path back to freedom. Rather than relying on elaborate cinematic storytelling, the game lets its setting and objectives gradually reveal the larger conflict, creating a focused narrative that complements its gameplay instead of overshadowing it.

The defining feature of Retool is its sophisticated hacking system, which serves as the foundation of nearly every challenge. Instead of treating hacking as a simple minigame, it becomes an integral tool for manipulating the environment. Players gain access to computer terminals that allow them to reroute electronic systems, opening locked doors, disabling security measures, activating machinery, or creating entirely new paths through each station. Every level becomes a puzzle that rewards observation and logical thinking, encouraging players to study the layout before deciding how best to overcome obstacles. This emphasis on experimentation keeps progression engaging, as success often comes from understanding how interconnected systems can be used creatively rather than relying solely on quick reflexes.

Stealth plays an equally important role throughout the adventure. Enemy patrols, surveillance devices, and hostile defenses require careful planning, making every encounter feel deliberate. However, the game avoids forcing players into a single playstyle. While remaining undetected is often the safest approach, Maria also has access to weapons for situations where direct confrontation becomes unavoidable. This flexibility allows players to adapt their tactics according to the circumstances, switching between careful infiltration and combat when necessary. The balance between these approaches keeps the pacing varied and ensures that missions rarely feel repetitive, even as the complexity of the stations gradually increases.

Another standout mechanic is the cloning system, which offers a refreshing alternative to traditional checkpoint design. Instead of severely punishing failure, the game encourages players to learn from their mistakes and continue experimenting with different strategies. This design philosophy removes much of the frustration commonly associated with trial-and-error puzzle solving, making exploration and creative problem-solving far more enjoyable. Character progression is further supported by upgrade opportunities that enhance Maria's hacking abilities, while collectible cosmetic hats provide an entertaining incentive for completionists who enjoy uncovering optional content scattered throughout the stations.

Visually, Retool adopts a clean three-dimensional presentation that emphasizes functionality over graphical spectacle. The damaged orbital facilities successfully capture the atmosphere of abandoned industrial space stations, with machinery, corridors, and electronic systems reinforcing the game's futuristic setting. Although the visuals remain relatively modest compared to larger productions, the environmental design prioritizes clarity, ensuring that interactive objects and important pathways are easy to identify. Complementing the presentation is a fitting electronic soundtrack that reinforces the isolation and tension of exploring hostile territory, enhancing both quiet moments of infiltration and more dangerous encounters.

The game also includes several quality-of-life features that broaden its appeal. Support for Steam achievements, cloud saves, trading cards, and multiple operating systems adds convenience and replay value, while the relatively accessible system requirements make it easy for a wide audience to experience. More importantly, Retool succeeds because it commits fully to its unique gameplay identity. Instead of imitating traditional action or stealth games, it builds its progression around environmental manipulation, logical thinking, and player creativity, resulting in an experience that feels consistently fresh from beginning to end.

Retool stands out as a thoughtful and engaging indie title that successfully blends hacking mechanics, stealth gameplay, environmental puzzles, and light combat into a cohesive science fiction adventure. Its strongest qualities come from giving players meaningful freedom to approach challenges in multiple ways while rewarding experimentation instead of punishing failure. Although its production values reflect its independent origins, the originality of its mechanics and the satisfying puzzle design make it an experience well worth exploring for fans of tactical, methodical gameplay.

Rating: 5/10
